propositions: Commit messages with body lines exceeding 72 characters or subjects exceeding 50 characters must be rejected at commit time with output naming each offending line and its length.

The commit-msg hook must be wired at the commit-msg stage (not pre-commit stage) and must not overwrite Gerrit's existing commit-msg hook; instead it chains as commit-msg.legacy in migration mode so Change-Id stamping is preserved.

Body lines are exempt from the 72-column check when they match trailers (^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9-]*:\s), tags (^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*=), fenced code blocks (^\s*```), indented literal blocks (raw line starts with 4+ spaces or tab), table rows (^\|), or atomic tokens (URL/path/dotted identifier longer than 72 chars where the remaining stripped line is ≤72).
The checker must never mutate the commit message and must ignore git scaffolding (comment lines starting with # and the --verbose diff below the >8 marker).
The Makefile make hooks target must verify both pre-commit and commit-msg hook files are present (exit non-zero if absent) and warn (but exit zero) if no Change-Id is detected in the hook chain.
